neighboring_unit_entries.title: Absolute convergence and unique factorization turn the integer series into a prime product
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Finite products of geometric series enumerate exactly the integers with bounded prime factors; a convergent tail estimate then passes to the infinite Euler product and separates arithmetic from analytic representations.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A truncated Perron kernel approximately inverts a Dirichlet series with frequency-controlled error
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Residue evaluation of y^s/s constructs an approximate step function; summing it against arbitrary coefficients yields an inversion formula whose error shrinks as the vertical frequency window widens.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The von Mangoldt weight is chosen so every prime power produced by differentiating an Euler factor contributes the same logarithmic prime weight. This makes the weighted prime count the coefficient-side representation of -zeta'/zeta, where zeros later become poles.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Lambda(n) equals log p on prime powers and zero otherwise, and Psi(x)=sum_{n<=x}Lambda(n) differs from the log-weighted prime sum by a controlled prime-power error. In Re(s)>1, uniform absolute convergence justifies differentiating the logarithm of the Euler product termwise, giving sum Lambda(n)n^{-s}=-zeta'(s)/zeta(s). The Euler product also proves zeta is nonzero there.
directed.conceptual_reading: The weighting is an interface design choice: it absorbs the repeated prime powers inherent in logarithmic differentiation, replacing an awkward prime-only series by one exactly matched to analytic singularities.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Lambda is the coefficient bridge between Euler factors and the logarithmic derivative; Psi is its cumulative arithmetic observable; -zeta'/zeta will expose zeros as poles.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The identity and nonvanishing argument depend on absolute and uniform convergence in Re(s)>1. Psi is only approximately a prime count and includes all prime powers.
directed.uncertainty: The convergence checks and formulas are legible; the unit ends before developing the promised role of zeros.

section_entries.label: 4. Proof of the Prime Number Theorem
section_entries.mathematical_role: Proves a weak zero-free region and uses a matched contour shift and error balance to derive a quantitative PNT.

unit_result_entry.title: A zero-free strip is the exact contour resource needed for a quantitative prime number theorem
unit_result_entry.why_material: The theorem pair makes the causal channel explicit: excluding zeros only slightly left of one permits a contour shift and already yields a strong asymptotic for weighted primes.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Records the target before the separate construction of the strip and contour proof.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Slow phase variation upgrades the zeta approximation to the full right half-plane
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A van der Corput lemma compares a slowly oscillating sum with its integral; applied to the logarithmic phase, it cancels the tail of zeta and produces a length-|t| Dirichlet polynomial with O(x^-sigma) error.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A nonnegative trigonometric combination of Euler products prevents zeta from becoming too small near one
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The identity 3+4 cos(theta)+cos(2 theta)>=0 couples zeta at three heights; pole growth and vertical bounds then force a quantitative lower bound that transfers a short distance left of one.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The theorem pair isolates the causal resource for PNT: even a narrow zero-free strip crossing the one-line, together with a reciprocal-zeta bound, is enough to shift the prime-counting contour and obtain subexponential error.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 4.1 states Psi(x)=x with an error x exp(-c log^{1/10}x), and derives pi(x) asymptotic to Li(x). Theorem 4.3 supplies 1/zeta(s)=O(log^7(|t|+2)) and hence no zeros when sigma>=1-c/log^9(|t|+2). The source notes that this is only a slight extension of the Euler-product zero-free half-plane but includes Re(s)=1 and suffices for the quantitative PNT.
